sentences.text: Atlascopcosaurus was a small, plant-eating basal iguanodont dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Early Cretaceous.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial upper jaw with teeth, alongside referred specimens of teeth, another maxilla, and dentaries.
Because most of its skeleton is unknown, scientists infer it was a small, bipedal herbivore based on closely related species.
The genus name honors the Atlas Copco Company, which supplied equipment for the excavation where the dinosaur was found.
The specific name loadsi honors William Loads, the state manager for Atlas Copco who assisted during the excavation.
The type specimen was discovered in 1984 at the Dinosaur Cove East site on the coast of Victoria, Australia.
Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich named and described the species Atlascopcosaurus loadsi in 1989.

Atlascopcosaurus was originally assigned to the family Hypsilophodontidae in 1988, but this group is now considered unnatural and polyphyletic, with the species viewed as a basal member of Euornithopoda.
Boyd (2015) considered the genus valid and placed it at the base of Iguanodontia in a clade with Anabisetia, Gasparinisaura, and Qantassaurus.
The time range for Atlascopcosaurus is estimated from the Barremian to the Albian stages, between 125.77 and 110.1 million years ago.
